ruleName: What You Can and Cannot Do in Bunkers
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic illustration in a junior golf quiz style. Show a golfer in a bunker preparing to hit a shot, with the clubhead brushing the grassy face of the bunker during the backswing. The golf ball should be clearly in the sand near the grass. Focus on showing the moment the clubhead touches the grass, not the sand. The scene should look about 75% realistic and 25% stylised, appealing and clear. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer in a bunker taking a backswing, with the clubhead brushing the grass face of the bunker. The golf ball sits in the sand near the grass.

sceneSpec.setting: A well-maintained golf course bunker with a grassy face around its edge.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer, Jezz, is in the bunker preparing for a shot.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball lies in the sand near the grass face of the bunker.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Jezz’s clubhead is brushing the grass on the bunker face during his backswing.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Shows that touching grass, but not sand, with the club in the bunker is allowed during the backswing.
mustShow: Golfer in bunker making a backswing with clubhead brushing the grass face
Ball clearly lying in the sand near the grass face
mustNotShow: Text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles

questions.title: Hitting Grass on the Side of a Bunker When Swinging Back
questions.question: Jezz is in a bunker. When he swings his club back to hit the ball, his club touches the long grass on the side of the bunker. What happens?

choices.text: There is no penalty for Jezz.
The ball must go back and Jezz tries again.

questions.explanation: In golf, you are not allowed to touch the sand in a bunker with your club before hitting the ball, but it is okay if your club touches just the grass on the side when you swing back. There is no penalty for this.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A bunker is a special sandy area on the golf course. You usually have to hit the ball out of the sand.
The backswing is when you swing your club backwards before you hit the ball.

questions.teachingTip: Use a practice bunker and show children swinging back so their club touches grass, but not sand. Discuss which actions have penalties and which do not.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think touching any part of the bunker, even grass, is always a penalty.
They might believe that hitting grass is the same as hitting sand in the bunker.

questions.title: Striking Grass on the Bunker Face with the Club on the Backswing
questions.question: Jezz takes a stroke from a bunker and strikes the grass face with his clubhead on the backswing. What is the ruling?

choices.text: The ball is to be replaced and the stroke replayed.

questions.explanation: Rule 12.2b only restricts certain acts involving touching sand in the bunker. Accidentally striking grass on the bunker face during the backswing is permitted.
